points.t: A **small painful crusted nodule on the helix or antihelix**, worse lying on that side, in an older adult.
**Pressure on cartilage** with poor blood supply → inflammation and cartilage damage (‘a pressure sore of the ear’).
**Pressure-relief pillow / ear protector for 4–6 weeks**; consider potent topical steroid; refer if failing or atypical.
**SCC or BCC of the ear**; **keratoacanthoma** (rapid crater); **tophaceous gout**.

cause.lead: A pressure sore of the ear cartilage.
points: Little padding and poor blood supply over cartilage.
Sustained pressure (sleeping on one side, headsets, phones, hats, CPAP), cold, sun damage → perichondritis → focal cartilage necrosis that extrudes.

visuals.caption: Chondrodermatitis: a tender crusted nodule on the upper ear rim. First line is offloading with a foam ear protector or pillow with a hole, for at least 4–6 weeks.
visuals.alt: Ear with a crusted rim nodule beside a foam ring pillow

points: Firm round **4–10 mm** nodule with a **central crust, scale or keratin plug**; may ulcerate.
**Wakes them at night** lying on it; light squeeze → disproportionate pain.
Helix (men) or antihelix (women), on the **side slept on**.
Dermoscopy is non-specific: **can’t exclude SCC / BCC**.
Which side do they sleep on? Headsets, CPAP?
Squeeze test; palpate pre-auricular / cervical nodes.
Rapid growth, bleeding, induration, > 1 cm, pearly edge, **painless**, no improvement after **6–8 weeks** offloading, immunosuppression, anxiety.
If tophi suspected (not in a flare).

cards.name: cSCC
cards.clue: Indurated, keratotic / ulcerated, growing; often painless ± node.

cards.name: Chilblain / relapsing polychondritis
cards.clue: Cold, bilateral / whole ear red sparing lobe.

points: **Foam ear protector** (OTC / online), pillow with a hole or travel pillow; sleep on the other side; remove headset / phone pressure.
At least a month; recurrence common if offloading stops.
Analgesia; emollient / protective dressing over the crust.
Potent topical steroid; intralesional triamcinolone (trained; atrophy risk) via GP / GPwSI / dermatology.
Failing or atypical: biopsy / surgery (cartilage excision).

limits.t: Don’t stop for minor skin surgery (BSDS 2023).

items.t: Rapidly growing, ulcerating or bleeding ear nodule, or with a nearby node: **suspected SCC** (NG12).
No improvement after 6–8 weeks of strict offloading: biopsy.

pearls.t: **Very painful at night** → CNH. **Painless and growing** → SCC / KA. Both can coexist.
Explain it as a pressure sore; adherence to offloading is the key.
Check immunosuppressant history (azathioprine, ciclosporin): SCC risk.

quiz.a: Painful ear nodule waking them when lying on that side.
Pressure relief (ear protector / pillow with a hole) for 4–6+ weeks.
Atypical features or no improvement after 6–8 weeks.

quiz.q: Painless rapidly growing crater on the ear?
